rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a standard multimodal setup with scgpt and resnet50 encoders, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion to establish a baseline performance. It is the best use of the first experiment to gather initial insights into multimodal effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (avgpool aggregation + concat fusion) achieved 0.512 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted while keeping other parameters the same, directly comparing aggregation methods. It clarifies whether weighted fusion improves performance over simple concatenation in this multimodal setup, a key design choice with potential for significant impact. This is the best use of the next experiment as it builds on the previous configuration while testing a critical component affecting model performance.

The existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_004) outperforms concat (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (while keeping scgpt+resnet50 and weighted fusion) further improves performance. It balances exploitation of the promising weighted fusion direction with exploration of aggregation methods, which could be critical for multimodal integration.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool and weighted fusion (as in config_004) yield the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (scgpt → scvi_n200) and image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while retaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. This clarifies whether advanced encoders can further improve performance, balancing exploration of encoder choices with exploitation of proven settings.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_007) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (used in config_007) with transformer aggregation and concat fusion could further improve performance. This clarifies whether alternative aggregation/fusion strategies can build on the strong foundation of scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of design choices.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_046) achieve high validation accuracy. This experiment tests a similar setup with pca_n2000 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation, which could clarify if the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) significantly impacts performance when paired with imagenet_vit_l. It balances exploration of RNA encoder alternatives with leveraging the strong image encoder from top performers.

The existing evidence shows config_046 (0.7207) is the top performer with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l. This experiment tests scgpt with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could improve accuracy by leveraging the high-performing image encoder with a different RNA encoder. It clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice impacts performance when using the effective image encoder and fusion method.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (e.g., config_046) achieve high accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests a similar setup (same encoders) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion instead of concat fusion, which could clarify if fusion method impacts performance. It balances exploration (testing a variant of a high-performing configuration) and exploitation (focusing on proven encoder combinations). This is the best use of the remaining budget to potentially improve upon the current best.

The existing evidence shows config_003 (0.725) is the top performer with multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. config_049 is the only untested configuration using scvi_n200 and weighted fusion (key factors in config_003's success) but with singleprofile and resnet50. This tests whether changing profile setting and image encoder could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of new combinations.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (e.g., config_003) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l but uses aggregation=None and fusion=weighted, which could clarify if removing aggregation improves performance. It is the best use of the last experiment as it explores a critical design choice (aggregation method) in a high-performing encoder pair.
